input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now reuses one shared statistics dict across calls and clears it on every invocation, so concurrent calls to the same decorated coroutine overwrite each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two overlapping awaits of the same decorated async function. Mechanism: the second call runs stats.clear() on the dict that the first call's copy also writes to, so the first call's attempt_number and other fields are reset or replaced by the second call's values. Previously each call got a fresh dict. Impact: callers reading wrapped_f.statistics or per-call stats during concurrent use see wrong or mixed values.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: a single shared statistics dict is cleared and reused on every call. Overlapping async calls then wipe or overwrite each other's attempt_number and other fields, leaving mixed statistics.
